change: Admission-pool experiment for 19 R-free direct-expression programs; candidate-only standalone P emission and compiler pool cost.

design.scope: Primary build and run results are separate. All 18 controls are build artifact controls; three of those also have exact-output run controls.
design.process_boundary: Fresh CLI child from launch through output/artifact completion and teardown; no phase subtraction.

primary_program_bytes.candidate_structural_contract: No scriptw_runtime imports, R sidecar, memory import/export, memory section, data section, or data_count section.

aa_descriptive_only.purpose: Identical-binary calibration; does not waive the prior append A/A failure.

gates.gate_note: Primary build/run median geomeans are gated per block. Every primary build must remain R-free with no memory/data/data-count section or memory import/export and candidate P <=25% of baseline. Control builds require exact P/R bytes. Any case/control timing or RSS veto is evaluated independently by mode.

test_correction.reason: Correct standalone test classification and legacy large-String memory assertion; production and frozen product unchanged.

test_only_correction.reason: Use admitted Boolean condition; replace the obsolete large Standalone String linear-memory expectation. Production inputs and compiler fingerprint unchanged.

limitations: The previous primitive-append experiment's failed A/A remains binding and is not waived by this experiment's descriptive A/A.
No V8 or Scriptc parity claim is made by these compiler build/run measurements.
Native verification is the exact selected scope in its receipt, not full Engine, workspace, Test262, or full ECMAScript acceptance.
Heap-backed build controls retain slower observations: join-mixed-1024 wall median rose about13% in block0; hello wall mean rose about7.8% in block1. Neither triggered a repeated timing veto.
Heap-backed run join4096 peak-RSS median rose3.912MiB in block0 (mean3.049MiB); no repeated4MiB median-and-mean RSS veto fired. Peak RSS is not live JS heap.
The benefit applies only to the existing tightly admitted runtime-free IR class. No runtime-admission rule, heap-backed program generation, runtime image, or V8/Scriptc execution cohort was changed.
Independent audit accepts only the recorded scopes; complete release, full Engine and pinned Test262 acceptance remain open.
